We just launched a tool today to physically measure this "Agentic Friction," but I'm curious what the community thinks: Should front-end devs be designing for human UI, or should they be stripping down their DOMs so AI agents can actually read and cite them? For founders launching today: Are you still investing in traditional SEO, or have you completely shifted your strategy to Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)? (P.S. We just launched GEO Stellar today to actually measure this friction would love to know what frameworks you're all using to stay visible to AI!). 👋 I'm Samir — a Tech & Cybersecurity Professor and the solo founder of GEO Stellar. GEO Stellar™ evaluates your site, or that of your client, exactly the way AI agents do, using a built-in deep-node scanner — measuring Agentic Friction™, identifying citation gaps, and handing you the exact code patches needed to win the new era of search. **Let's test your site right now:** Drop your URL in the comments below, and I'll run a manual deep-node scan and tell you live how "Agentic Ready" your site is! Or, if you are ready to secure your AI search advantage, click through to claim one of the 25 Founding Member spots. P.S. As a thank you to the Product Hunt community for the early support today, I'm doing a "Founder's Blitz" for the first 3 people who want to test the enterprise nodes. And I’ve already scheduled a meeting for tomorrow to discuss this with the team lead and the front-end developers.
